input: Look into pet insurance for the cat

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user wants a quick overview of options or a thorough comparison with a final recommendation changes how deep the research needs to go.
Details about the cat (age, breed, health history) directly affect which plans are available, what pre-existing conditions may be excluded, and the likely premium range.
A monthly budget ceiling immediately narrows which plans are worth considering and prevents wasted effort researching unaffordable options.
Some owners prioritise accident-only cover, others want comprehensive wellness and routine care — knowing this shapes which plan types to focus on.
The country and region determine which insurers operate there, any legal requirements, and the typical vet cost baseline the insurance needs to cover.
Understanding what outcome counts as 'done' — a shortlist, a single chosen plan, or an actually purchased policy — defines when the task is complete.
Knowing whether the user wants to do the research themselves with a guide, or wants a ready-made comparison laid out for them, determines the format of the output.

gold.taskTitle: Research and choose pet insurance for the cat
gold.taskDescription: Look into pet insurance options for the user's cat, comparing plans and providers to find the right coverage.

questions.title: How old is your cat, and does it have any known health conditions?
questions.description: Age and health history affect plan eligibility, premium cost, and pre-existing condition exclusions.

questions.title: What country or region are you based in?
questions.description: Location determines which insurers are available and the typical vet cost baseline being insured against.

questions.title: Do you have a monthly premium budget in mind?
questions.description: A budget ceiling immediately filters out unaffordable plans and focuses the research.

questions.title: What type of coverage matters most to you — accidents only, illness, or full wellness?
questions.description: The desired coverage type determines which plan categories to prioritise in the comparison.

questions.title: Do you want a broad overview of options or a single top recommendation?
questions.description: The desired depth of research changes whether to produce a shortlist or a definitive pick.

questions.title: What does 'done' look like — a shortlist, or a policy actually purchased?
questions.description: The end goal determines whether this task ends at research or continues through to enrollment.

questions.title: Would you prefer a structured comparison table or step-by-step guidance to research yourself?
questions.description: The preferred format shapes whether to deliver a ready-made output or a self-directed action plan.
